descripcion_es: Real or likely conditions in the future: if + present, will + infinitive.
resumen: The first conditional expresses a possible future situation and its consequence: If it rains, we'll stay at home. The if part takes the present, never will.

filas: If you see Ana, say hello.
If we hurry, we can catch the bus.

explicacion.texto: The two parts can go in either order. If the condition comes first, it is followed by a comma: If I have time, I'll call you. If the consequence comes first, there is usually no comma: I'll call you if I have time.
As in Spanish (“si llueve, nos quedaremos”), if is followed by the present: If it rains, not If it will rain.

items: Unless = if not: Unless you hurry, you'll miss the train (= If you don't hurry...).
When is used for something that will certainly happen: When I get home, I'll call you. If is for something possible: If I get the job, I'll celebrate.
The same rule applies after when, as soon as, before and after with a future meaning: I'll tell you as soon as I know.

ejemplos.frase: If you need anything, I'll be in my office.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si necesitas algo, estaré en mi despacho.

ejemplos.frase: If we leave now, we'll arrive on time.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si salimos ya, llegaremos a tiempo.

ejemplos.frase: She won't come if you don't invite her.
ejemplos.traduccion: No vendrá si no la invitas.

ejemplos.frase: What will you do if you lose your job?
If you're cold, close the window.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si tienes frío, cierra la ventana.

ejemplos.frase: Unless it stops raining, the match will be cancelled.
ejemplos.traduccion: Si no deja de llover, se suspenderá el partido.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: If it will rain, we'll stay at home.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: If it rains, we'll stay at home.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: After if use the present, not will.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: If you will help me, I finish early.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: If you help me, I'll finish early.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Will goes in the consequence, not in the condition.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I'll text you when I will arrive.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I'll text you when I arrive.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: After when with a future meaning you also use the present.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: If you ___ (eat) all that cake, you'll feel sick.
respuestas: eat
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the main rule in the card: the if part takes the present simple, never will. The clue is if, which introduces the condition, while the consequence already has will (you'll feel sick). With you the present simple is the base form: eat. It is the same as in Spanish, where we say “si te comes”, not “si te comerás”.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si te comes toda esa tarta, te sentirás mal.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Will is not used after if: the condition is in the present, eat.
With you the verb has no -s: eat.
The past would turn the sentence into a second conditional (If you ate…, you would…); with you'll the condition is in the present.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: If she misses the bus, she ___ (be) late.
respuestas: will be
'll be
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in the card shows that the consequence is formed with will + infinitive without to. The condition (If she misses the bus) is already in the present, so the gap is the future consequence: will be or the contraction 'll be. Will is the same for all persons, without -s.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si pierde el autobús, llegará tarde.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The future consequence needs will: she will be late.
After will comes the infinitive without to: will be.
Will is not followed by to: will be.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: We ___ (not / go) to the beach if the weather is bad.
respuestas: won't go
will not go
ejercicios.explicacion: According to the card, a negative consequence is formed with won't (will not) + infinitive. The condition if the weather is bad comes at the end and is in the present, which is correct: the card reminds you that the order can be reversed and that there is then usually no comma. That is why the gap is won't go or will not go.
ejercicios.traduccion: No iremos a la playa si hace mal tiempo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It expresses a habit; for the future consequence you need won't go.
After won't comes the infinitive without to: won't go.
After will not comes the base form, not -ing: will not go.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: If my brother ___ (get) the job, he'll move to Barcelona.
respuestas: gets
ejercicios.explicacion: The card says that if is followed by the present simple. My brother is third person singular, so the verb takes -s: gets. The consequence is already in the future (he'll move). Get the job means “to be given the job”. Spanish speakers sometimes forget the -s because they think of the condition as something hypothetical.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After if, present simple; third person with -s.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si mi hermano consigue el trabajo, se mudará a Barcelona.

errores_previstos.explicacion: The third person -s is missing: my brother gets.
Will is not used after if: gets.
The past belongs to the second conditional; with he'll in the consequence you use the present gets.

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete with the correct form of the verb.
ejercicios.frase: I'll phone you as soon as I ___ (land).
respuestas: land
ejercicios.explicacion: The card extends the if rule: after when, as soon as, before and after with a future meaning you also use the present. As soon as introduces a future moment, but the verb is in the present simple: land. With I it has no -s. In Spanish we use the subjunctive here (“aterrice”), and that pushes learners to use will, which is wrong.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After as soon as with a future meaning, use the present.

errores_previstos.explicacion: After as soon as with a future meaning you use the present, not will.
The landing is in the future: the present land is correct after as soon as.
For a single, brief action after as soon as you use the present simple: land.

ejercicios.frase: If you ___ me, I'll help you.
respuestas: ask
ejercicios.explicacion: This applies the central rule: the condition is in the present simple and the consequence takes will. The clue is if, which introduces the condition, and I'll help, which marks a first conditional. With you the form is ask, without -s. It is the typical structure of an offer or promise.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: The condition is in the present.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si me lo pides, te ayudaré.

por_opcion.ask: Correct: present simple in the condition of the first conditional.
por_opcion.will ask: Incorrect: will is not used after if in a normal conditional.
por_opcion.asked: It is past and would belong to the second conditional (If you asked me, I'd help you), which does not fit with I'll.

ejercicios.frase: You'll fail the exam ___ you study.
respuestas: unless
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that unless means if not. The sentence means “you will fail if you don't study”, but the verb study is affirmative, so the “not” has to be in the conjunction: unless. With if it would say the opposite of what is logical, “you will fail if you study”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Unless = if not: you will fail if you don't study.
ejercicios.traduccion: Suspenderás el examen a menos que estudies.

por_opcion.if: It would give an absurd meaning: “you will fail if you study”. To keep if you would have to say if you don't study.
por_opcion.when: When presents studying as certain and the result would be absurd: “you will fail when you study”.

ejercicios.frase: If they don't hurry, they ___ the train.
respuestas: will miss
ejercicios.explicacion: The condition is already in the present (If they don't hurry), so the future consequence must take will + infinitive: will miss. The clue is that miss the train is a result that has not happened yet. Miss here means “to be too late for” a means of transport.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si no se dan prisa, perderán el tren.

por_opcion.miss: The present would express a general truth (zero conditional); for a specific future consequence you need will.
por_opcion.will miss: Correct: will + infinitive for the future consequence.
por_opcion.missed: The past does not express a future consequence and does not combine with don't hurry.

ejercicios.frase: What will you do if it ___ tomorrow?
respuestas: snows
ejercicios.explicacion: The rule in the card still applies when the sentence starts with the consequence: after if, present simple. Tomorrow indicates the future, but that does not change the verb in the condition. The subject it is third person, so snow adds -s: snows. Will is already in the other part (What will you do).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: After if, present simple (third person: snows).

por_opcion.snows: Correct: present simple with third person -s after if.
por_opcion.will snow: Incorrect: even when talking about tomorrow, if is followed by the present.
por_opcion.snow: It is missing the third person -s that it requires.

ejercicios.enunciado: Join the two sentences with if, starting with If.
ejercicios.frase: You water the plants. They will grow.
respuestas: If you water the plants, they will grow.
If you water the plants, they'll grow.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card gives the pattern If + present, will + infinitive, and adds that when the condition comes first it is followed by a comma. The first sentence (You water the plants) becomes the condition, in the present, and the second the consequence with will. The contraction they'll is accepted. Water as a verb means “to give water to” plants.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: If + present, will + infinitive; comma after the condition.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If you will water the plants, they will grow.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will is not used after if: If you water…

errores_previstos.respuesta: If you water the plants, they grow.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The will in the consequence, which the original sentence had, has been lost.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If you water the plants, they will to grow.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After will comes the infinitive without to.

ejercicios.frase: If you don't leave now, you'll be late.
respuestas: Unless you leave now, you'll be late.
Unless you leave now, you will be late.
You'll be late unless you leave now.
You will be late unless you leave now.
ejercicios.explicacion: According to the card, unless means if not, so it replaces if… don't. When you change it, the verb becomes affirmative: if you don't leave → unless you leave. The consequence does not change. Versions with the consequence first are also accepted, and they usually have no comma.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Unless = if not; the verb is affirmative.
ejercicios.traduccion: A menos que te vayas ya, llegarás tarde.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Unless you don't leave now, you'll be late.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Double negative: unless already includes not, so the verb is affirmative.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Unless you will leave now, you'll be late.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After unless, as after if, you use the present.

errores_previstos.respuesta: Unless you leave now, you are late.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The future consequence needs will: you'll be late.

ejercicios.frase: If I will see Tom, I'll give him the message.
respuestas: If I see Tom, I'll give him the message.
If I see Tom, I will give him the message.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the mistake the card highlights most: after if comes the present simple, never will. You have to remove will from the condition: If I see Tom. The consequence, I'll give him the message, is correct. In Spanish we would not say “si veré a Tom” either.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si veo a Tom, le daré el mensaje.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I will see Tom, I'll give him the message.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: will is not used after if.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I see Tom, I give him the message.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The wrong will has been removed, but the future consequence does need it.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I will see Tom, I give him the message.
errores_previstos.explicacion: The mistake has been moved: will must be in the consequence, not after if.

ejercicios.frase: If you don't hurry, you miss the flight.
respuestas: If you don't hurry, you'll miss the flight.
If you don't hurry, you will miss the flight.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table in the card shows that the future consequence is expressed with will + infinitive. In the original sentence will is missing: you miss sounds like a general truth, not a specific consequence of this situation. You must say you'll miss or you will miss. The condition is already correct.
ejercicios.traduccion: Si no te das prisa, perderás el vuelo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If you don't hurry, you miss the flight.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: the future consequence needs will.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If you won't hurry, you'll miss the flight.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Will has been put in the condition: after if comes the present, don't hurry.

errores_previstos.respuesta: If you don't hurry, you'll missing the flight.
errores_previstos.explicacion: After will comes the infinitive without -ing: miss.

respuestas: I'll buy it if it's cheap
If it's cheap I'll buy it
ejercicios.explicacion: The card explains that the two parts can go in either order: consequence + if + condition, or if + condition + consequence. I'll buy it takes will and it's cheap is in the present after if. Both orders are accepted; in writing, with the condition first, you would add a comma.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Consequence with will + if + present, or the other way round.
ejercicios.traduccion: Lo compraré si es barato. (También: Si es barato, lo compraré.)

errores_previstos.respuesta: If I'll buy it it's cheap
errores_previstos.explicacion: If must introduce the condition (it's cheap), not the consequence with will.

errores_previstos.respuesta: It's cheap if I'll buy it
errores_previstos.explicacion: The meaning has been reversed: the condition is that it is cheap, and will does not go after if.

descripcion_larga_es: The first conditional expresses a possible future condition and its consequence: If it rains, we'll stay at home. It works almost the same as in Spanish (“si llueve, nos quedaremos”): present after if and future in the consequence. That is why the typical mistake is not one of logic but of form: putting will after if or after when and as soon as, and confusing unless with “a menos que no”.

contexto.que_es: It is a two-part structure: the condition, introduced by if with the verb in the present simple, and the consequence, usually with will + infinitive, an imperative or a modal. It describes something that can really happen in the future.
contexto.por_que_importa: It is used to warn, promise, negotiate, threaten or plan, functions that are very frequent in a conversation or in a presentation about policies and their effects (If the central bank raises rates, inflation will fall). Putting will after if is one of the most visible mistakes at intermediate level. Confusing if with when or unless changes the degree of certainty or reverses the meaning.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: When talking about a likely result of a real future situation. The signals are if, unless, when, as soon as, before and after with a future meaning. Spanish speakers get the present right after “si”, but with “cuando” they would use the subjunctive and tend to translate it with will (when I will arrive), and sometimes leave out will in the consequence (you miss the flight).
